core_obligations: For (1), record the exactness properties of f^{-1}: it preserves the final object and the empty sheaf, commutes with products and equalizers, and transforms isomorphisms and surjections into isomorphisms and surjections (proof lines 7824-7828).

Conclude that f^{-1} transports the characterizing isomorphism and surjection of the locally ringed condition to the pulled-back structure sheaf, so that (C', f^{-1}O) is locally ringed (proof lines 7829-7832).
proof_roadmap: List the exactness properties of the inverse image functor.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the locally ringed condition is intrinsic: pulling back the structure sheaf along any morphism of topoi preserves it, and an equivalence of ringed topoi preserves it in both directions. The proof derives the second statement from the first, and proves the first by collecting the exactness properties of the inverse image functor: it preserves the final object and the empty sheaf, commutes with products and equalizers, and carries isomorphisms and surjections to isomorphisms and surjections, so it transports both the isomorphism expressing that one is never zero and the surjectivity established in the equivalent characterization of the locally ringed condition (proof lines 7822-7832). H2: the transport of the two characterizing conditions through the exactness properties of the inverse image is the substance.
